topicTitle: Advanced Test Isolation: Mocks, Spies & MSW

lessons.title: Mocking Functions & Modules (vi.fn, vi.mock)
lessons.description: Replace real dependencies with controlled fakes to test code in isolation.

sections.heading: Why mock?
paragraphs: Unit tests should test your code, not its dependencies. Mocks replace external services, APIs and modules with controlled fakes that behave predictably.
list: vi.fn() — creates a mock function you can configure
Mock functions track calls, arguments and return values
Essential for testing code with side effects

codeExamples.heading: Mocking functions and modules
explanation: vi.fn() creates a function that tracks calls and arguments.
vi.mock() replaces entire modules with controlled fakes.
This ensures tests are isolated and predictable.

practice.task: Mock a fetch function and test a function that calls it. Verify the mock was called with the correct arguments.
hints: Pass the mock to your function.

keyTakeaways: Mocks replace real dependencies with controlled fakes.
vi.mock() replaces entire modules for isolated testing.
Always assert that mocks were called with expected arguments.
lessons.challenge: Test a payment processing function by mocking the payment gateway, email service and database.

lessons.title: Spying on Methods (vi.spyOn) & Manipulating Timers
lessons.description: Observe method calls without replacing them, and control time in tests for predictable results.

sections.heading: Spies and fake timers
list: vi.spyOn(obj, "method") — watches calls without replacing the method

codeExamples.heading: Spies and fake timers
explanation: Spies observe method calls without changing behavior.
Fake timers let you fast-forward time in tests.
advanceTimersByTime() runs all timers scheduled within that period.
Always restore real timers after using fake ones.

practice.task: Test a debounce function using fake timers. Verify it waits the specified delay before calling the callback.

keyTakeaways: Spies observe method calls without replacing the original behavior.
Fake timers let you control time in tests — no real waiting.
Always restore real timers and spies after each test.
lessons.challenge: Test an interval that increments a counter every second — verify 10 increments after advancing 10 seconds.

lessons.title: Intercepting Network Requests via Mock Service Worker (MSW)
lessons.description: Intercept real network requests at the network level — no code changes needed in your application.

sections.heading: What is MSW?
paragraphs: Mock Service Worker intercepts requests at the network level using a Service Worker. Your application makes real fetch calls — MSW intercepts them and returns fake responses.
list: Intercepts requests at the network level — no code changes needed
Works in both browser and Node.js
Define request handlers for specific URLs and methods
Supports JSON, images, errors and delayed responses

codeExamples.heading: MSW setup and handlers
explanation: MSW intercepts fetch requests before they leave the browser.
Handlers match URL patterns and return fake responses.
Your application code doesn't change — MSW works transparently.
Supports all HTTP methods and status codes.

practice.task: Set up MSW to intercept a fetch call and return mock data. Test that your application displays the mocked data correctly.
hints: Define handlers for your API endpoints.
Start MSW in your test setup or browser.

keyTakeaways: MSW intercepts network requests at the network level — no code changes needed.
Define handlers for specific URL patterns and HTTP methods.
Works transparently — your application makes real fetch calls.
Perfect for testing API-dependent code without hitting real servers.
lessons.challenge: Build a complete test suite for a data-fetching component using MSW to mock all API endpoints.
